methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $114M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sage Geosystems is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Cindy Taff and Lance Cook that has raised $114M+ to date. Valuation analysis relies on a comparable universe of three private peers in the same sector at Series C stage—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—alongside one public comparable and a broader frontier-tech peer set of eight private companies including Helion and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $114M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $217M. Peer-median valuation anchors to the three same-sector comparables, which have a median valuation of $1.0B, a floor of $700M, and a ceiling of $3.0B. The peer range reflects material heterogeneity in stage and capital efficiency across the cohort.

Triangulating these methods produces a low estimate of $184M, a median of $608M, and a high of $1.1B. The wide range reflects genuine uncertainty: stage-progression methodology alone—more conservative and capital-based—sits well below peer medians, suggesting either that Sage commands a valuation discount to comparable-stage peers or that peer comps trade at stage-inflation premiums. Resolution of this gap depends on customer traction, differentiation in core technology, and capital efficiency metrics not present in the current data set.
